transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I keep getting this thought that I missed something during my safety check on the cab, even when I know I did it. Then I worry somebody could get hurt, or my boss will think I lied. I can’t get it to stop while I’m driving or trying to study.
When that thought hits, do you go back and check the cab again?

Yeah. Before I can take a ride, I keep going around the cab checking the tires, lights, doors, meter, and paperwork again and again. Sometimes I take pictures, and if it still doesn’t feel right, I restart the whole check. Passengers can be waiting and I’m already late, but I can’t just leave.
Do you feel that the amount of checking you do is excessive, even though you still feel unable to stop?

Yeah, I know it’s too much. I’ll check the tires, lights, doors, meter, paperwork—then go back and do it again. Even if people are waiting and I’m late, I can’t leave until it feels right. Sometimes I take pictures or just start the whole check over.
Do you get the same kind of unwanted doubt-and-checking in other parts of your life besides the cab safety check?

It’s mostly around the car before a ride. I go over the tires, lights, doors, meter, and paperwork repeatedly. Sometimes I take pictures, and if I still don’t feel sure, I start the whole thing over—even when passengers are waiting and I’m late.
Before you start checking the cab, do you get an unwanted thought that something was missed or that someone could be harmed?

Yeah. Even after I’ve done the safety check, I get this thought that I missed something on the cab and somebody could get hurt. Or that my boss will think I lied about checking it. It just keeps going in my head.
When that thought comes up, is it mainly a fear that someone could be harmed because you missed something?

Yeah, mostly. I keep thinking I missed something on the cab and someone could get hurt because of me. And then I worry my boss will think I lied about doing the check. I know I checked, but I can’t make the thought stop, even when I’m driving or trying to study.
Do you check the cab to make the anxiety from that thought go down?

Yeah. I keep checking because I’m trying to make sure it’s safe and feel certain I didn’t miss anything. I’ll go around the tires, lights, doors, meter, paperwork again and again. Sometimes I take pictures, but if it still doesn’t feel right, I restart the whole check, even if passengers are waiting and I’m already late.
When that doubt comes up, are there times you do not go back and check, and the thought just stays in your mind?

Sometimes I try not to go back, but then it just stays in my head. I’ll be driving or trying to study, and I keep thinking I missed something and somebody could get hurt, or my boss will say I lied. I know I did the check, but I can’t get the thought to shut up.
Besides checking the cab, do you have any other repetitive rituals or mental habits you feel driven to do?

It’s mostly the checking. Before I take a ride, I keep going around the car—tires, lights, doors, the meter, paperwork—over and over. Sometimes I take pictures, but then I’ll think it still wasn’t right and start the whole thing again, even if people are waiting and I’m late.
About how much time do these checking thoughts and repeated safety checks take up in a typical day?

A lot of it—hours, probably. It makes me late getting on the road, and I’ve lost rides and gotten warnings because of it. Then my CDL studying gets pushed back because so much of the day is gone. I barely see my friends anymore either, because I’m behind on work or trying to catch up.
Do these unwanted thoughts about having missed something come back over and over even before you start checking the cab?

Yeah. It comes back before I even start checking. I’ll think I missed something on the cab, like somebody could get hurt or my boss will think I lied, even though I know I’m supposed to do the check. It just keeps hitting me and I can’t shut it off.
